## Revised B1 candidate (Option A)

> Read through the RAT lens already applied in this study (Hughes et al., 2006), the group contrast reported above is analytically useful: it situates each design relative to prior classroom activity rather than scoring teachers as persons. That framing alone, however, does not settle how the contrast should be interpreted theoretically. A substantial line of work on technology integration treats pedagogical knowledge developed in practice as central to sophisticated redesign and, on that basis, would lead one to expect in-service teachers to display at least comparable—and often greater—capacity for innovative technology use than pre-service teachers (Mishra & Koehler, 2006). Under that expectation, the observation as framed by RAT sits in partial tension with an experience-based understanding of innovative capacity. The task of this discussion is therefore not to restate coding outcomes, but to interpret a pattern that RAT makes visible yet that practice-centered accounts of innovative capacity leave under-explained.

**~155 words.** Friction is now only Theory 2 vs framed observation—not a restated finding.
